title: Recording, mixing: Single Pigeon by Wings | 1973
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Richard Lush

Wings completed ‘Single Pigeon’ on 29 January 1973, the final recording session for Red Rose Speedway.

The song was mostly recorded at Olympic Sound Studios on 9 March 1972. It was revived and finished on this day.

It was an unusual session, involving the members of Wings playing unconventional instruments: Paul McCartney played a trombone, Denny Laine was on saxophone, and Denny Seiwell played a cornet.

I went to Portobello Road, where they have a big flea market, and I bought this beautiful old Besson cornet. It came in a beat-up old leather bag, and it was really screwed up. And I said, ‘How much do you want for that?’ And I gave him a couple of pounds and went home, and had it worked on a little bit, so that it played OK. I brought it to the session one day, and it’s on ‘Single Pigeon’.
Denny Seiwell
Red Rose Speedway Deluxe Edition, 2018

‘Single Pigeon’ was mixed in stereo in six attempts towards the end of the session.

Page last updated: 27 November 2025
